utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was the video-clip Exhibit 2D71. Your Honours, as it was proven during the Prosecution case and will be shown during the Defence case, the so-called NLA did not have organisational capacities. The so-called rule books that the Prosecution presented as evidence for the organisation were nothing more but a copy/pasted rule books of the Kosovo Protection Corps, and its authors did not even bother to change the name from Kosovo to Macedonia. There's no reliable evidence that these rules were ever implemented, and even if they had been, that they had had any impact or relevance on the functioning of the so-called NLA. These regulations were a propaganda tool to give a criminal organisation the appearance of a military body. As the so-called chief of General Staff of the NLA, Gzim Ostreni, testified that he did not even know whether the headquarters were in Selce, Sipkovica, or Prizren in Kosovo. Did he not know the number of his forces, what kind of communications they used, and so forth. Even the so-called chief of the General Staff of the NLA did not issue even a single order, as he testified. This proves that the organisation of the so-called NLA was imaginary and for purposes of presenting the NLA as not being a terrorist organisation. Your Honours, the so-called NLA did not have the ability to conduct any kind of serious attack on the Macedonian forces. They could not do so because they neither had the organisation to do so, nor the structure, nor logistics of their forces. They committed criminal attacks that only a small group of criminals can do. The only thing they were able to do was to ambush convoys or plant mines on normal roads used by everyone and then to retreat either back to Kosovo or in some villages inhabited by Albanians. Such ambushes were carried out by no more than 10 to 15 terrorists at a time. They never lasted more than several minutes. The problem of the Macedonian security forces then was to search and destroy the terrorists, because they would hide in Albanian villages, hid their uniforms, and became innocent civilians. This was the tactics that the NLA was successful in implementing, the only one they were successful in implementing. The problem of the Macedonian security forces was that they were too careful not to target civilians. Even they knew that there are terrorists hiding from the Macedonian security forces, as a result of which they would hesitate to attack. Your Honours, the so-called NLA never held any territory. They would suddenly appear in some mountain villages populated with Albanians. They would come out to have a photo taken and would disappear. On several occasions when they confronted the security forces, like in Tetovo, in March 2001, in Vaksince in May 2001, in Aracinovo in June 2001, and Ljuboten in 2001, they withdrew and be destroyed. What the Prosecutor describes as control of territory was nothing but a rule of fear and violence by expelling non-Albanians and frightened the Albanians who did not support them. It would be a terrible precedent if such criminal activities were to form the grounds of finding of this Court that an armed conflict existed. The violence was spread only on the territory that was bordering Kosovo. The terrorists did not have the capacity to make a coordinated action even in this territory. The whole episode of events lasted for only four to five months without any terrorist activities in the month of April 2001. Your Honours, the goal of these criminals was to separate the territory of Macedonia and to unite it with Kosovo. This goal failed. The Macedonian security forces succeeded in defending Macedonia and for the first time in the modern Macedonian history they succeeded in defending its territory from being chunked away by its neighbours. Now I would like to move to the events in Ljuboten. During the crisis, the village of Ljuboten was used as an important logistic place for the so-called NLA. The presence of the NLA in the village occurred long before these events and continued long after these events. As numerous witnesses of the Prosecution witnessed, Ljuboten was used to smuggle arms, food, and medicines for the need of the NLA, especially for those that were stationed in the Kumanovo region and the village of Matejce. Your Honours, well before the crisis started in 2001 and after the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, the Albanian armed groups were present in the village of Ljuboten. What the Prosecution is trying to say is that although there were armed Albanian activities in Ljuboten before and after the events, magically no such presence was registered during that weekend. That simply is not reasonable and is contrary to the evidence. There had always been an armed presence of the NLA in the village. Due to the strategic importance the NLA decided not to raise the flag but to remain under covert control. The Macedonian security forces were aware of this situation, and in June 2001 the army surrounded the village of Ljuboten, in order to be able to put it under its observation or, to use the army terminology, to be on a higher level, if something happens. Now, I would like to quote Exhibit 1D31, which is the standard operating procedure on the OSCE Monitoring Mission. Start of quote: "The modus operandi of the ethnic Albanian armed groups by and large is to occupy ground by infiltrating requiring a great deal of preparations before overtly declaring areas under their control. These preparations include the insertion of supplies, arms, and equipment as well as preparation of the local inhabitants to be receptive to their emergence. Therefore, there are a number of indicators, the hardening of the local population's attitude to the government, lots of young men hanging around looking suspiciously or the noticeably enhanced security stance of Macedonian forces in the area which could suggest that an area is being prepared to be taken over or is ready. The sudden exodus of women and children from the village is also a strong indicator that the activity of the armed groups of ethnic Albanians is imminent. Normally, these preparations are done in the regions where there is a significant population of ethnic Albanians." In June 2001, the so-called NLA decided to try to conduct terrorist attacks on the capital of Skopje. First, the NLA occupied the village of Aracinovo and threatened to shell its refinery, the airport, and the parliament; Exhibit 2D37 and 2D38, however, with a swift operation and NATO assistance they were neutralised. Then the NLA infiltrated two groups clad as civilians in the city of Skopje in order to start street fights which is Exhibit 2D41. Some of the members of the NLA that were dressed in civilian clothes were caught and neutralized by the Macedonian security forces taking shelter in Albanian houses in the suburb of Cair which is one kilometre away from the city centre. Exhibit P364. Since the village of Ljuboten was surrounded by Macedonian forces the NLA main forces from the Lipkovo area were unable to enter the village. In addition to the situation the destruction of the existing supply channels of the armed Albanian extremists in the area of Nikustak and Matejce where the departure of the security forces from the check-points would have allowed an uninterrupted passage of armed groups from the area of Nikustak and Matejce and the emerging with the groups of armed Albanian extremists in the area of Radusa, which is why, on the 10th of August, 2001, the villagers of Ljuboten who were members of the NLA led by Shefajet Bajrami, the brother of the deceased Sulejman and Xhelal Bajrami, planted two mines on the outgoing shift of soldiers that were stationed above the village of Ljuboten, which resulted in the death of eight innocent Macedonian reservist soldiers. On the same date, a battalion of the NLA from Lipkovo received orders to enter the village of Ljuboten. The Macedonian army intelligence units, on the 10th of August, at the 1655, intercepted the information and passed it through the chain of command; Exhibit 2D42. At the same time, the villagers of Ljubanci and Radisani, afraid that they would be attacked next, demanded weapons to be able to defend themselves. On the 10th of August, 2001, immediately after the mine incident, the army stationed at the position above Ljuboten noticed several NLA members wearing black uniforms and entering the village of Ljuboten from the direction of Ljubotenski Bacila and they opened machine and sniper fire, which resulted with the death of at least two terrorists and retreat of the others behind the high walls of the Albanian houses; exhibit P301, corroborated by few Prosecution witnesses and two Defence witnesses. The situation was very tense and could be described as dramatic. At the same time, the NLA was conducting ethnic cleansing in Macedonian villages in the area of Tetovo. It was kidnapping and killing civilians, torturing many more. This can be found in the OSCE report, Exhibit 1D267 and Exhibit 1D268, 1D16. As the OSCE special report on complaints about human rights related to the armed groups of ethnic Albanians in the Tetovo area, which is Exhibit 1D18, notes: "The mission specialist confirmed the reports from the OSCE monitors in the Tetovo area that even during the cease-fire the ethnic Macedonian civilian population north of Tetovo is under heavy pressure from the armed groups of ethnic Albanians to leave. The pressure is in the form of kidnapping, temporary detentions and serious and persistent forms of intimidation and restriction of the movement of the civilians who try to be engaged in ordinary activities such as agricultural activities, shopping or going to work. The conduct of the armed groups of ethnic Albanians is consistent with an attempt to ethnically cleanse this area." The same happened in Kumanovo, where local Macedonians and others were ethnically cleansed by the NLA and have not returned to their homes to this date. The same was done by the terrorists in Skopje, in the village of Aracinovo, where all Macedonian houses were burned down and the Macedonians still live in temporary shelters to this date. Due to the gravity of the situation the Macedonian Security Council met on the 10th of August, 2001, and demanded a firm action; Exhibit 1D249. Your Honours, as it will be explained by the military expert, after the killing of the ten Macedonian soldiers in Karpalak, again in ambush as the Prosecution witness Henry Bolton testified, 300 kilograms of explosives were planted under the highway, Tetovo-Skopje. The supreme commander, Mr. Boris Trajkovski, dismissed from duty the chief of the military staff -- of the General Staff; Exhibit 2D84. Furthermore, the order of the president of Macedonia to destroy the NLA on the highway [as interpreted] Tetovo-Jazince - it should be road in the transcript, not a highway - leaked from the military staff and was made public on the national TV which is why the plan failed. However strange it may appear at first glance, the preparations for the action were conducted in conspirative manner and only among those that should have been its direct perpetrators, the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade and the department for internal affairs in Cair for the action in the village of Ljuboten. This was logical. It has to be taken into account that the plan to attack the Tetovo-Jazince road on the 5th of August, 2001 leaked to the media by some of the top military commanders and the chief of the General Staff was revoked on the 10th of August, 2001. A new one was not appointed and the preparations demanded a certain degree of planning. As this was the case for Ljuboten, in such abnormal circumstances, the president of Macedonia ordered that the police and the army jointly defend of village of Ljubanci and the access to Skopje and, should it be necessary, to attack; Exhibit P303. He ordered Tarculovski to monitor the situation and to inform him about it. On that date, members of the police arrived in the village of Ljubanci and held a meeting with the army, on which meeting various options were discussed. The president of Macedonia had all the necessary intelligence information. He had information that the NLA battalion was trying to enter the village of Ljuboten to reinforce the present members of the NLA which were located there. The president had information that after the mine incident the members of the NLA withdrew in the village of Ljuboten and made defensive positions. He had information who the NLA members in the village were as well as of the fact that there were terrorists in the village. Every structure of the army and the police had information that Ljuboten was a village which was full of NLA members and that many villagers from Ljuboten were NLA members too. These forces remained under the full authority of the president of the country. Even OSCE had information that the NLA had a covert presence in Ljuboten; Exhibit 1D23. There was no initial plan to enter the village of Ljuboten which didn't happen, probably because the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, Major Despodov was awaiting further orders from his superiors. Consequently on the night of the 11th of August, 2001, between 18 and 19 hours a telephone conversation took place between President Trajkovski and Major Mitre Despodov through Johan Tarculovski. It is important to take into account the legislation for the service in the army. I quote: "A military officer has the obligation to execute the order of a superior that relates to his fulfilment of service. A military officer is also obliged to execute the orders of a senior officer if his immediate superior officer is not present and when necessary measures must be undertaken to complete urgent and significant tasks." In this case, President Trajkovski asked the supreme commander could give an order to Major Despodov who would have the obligation to execute it. If this had been the case, the attack would have commenced on Saturday, on the 11th of August, 2001. However, during a moment of tension on Sunday, 12th August, 2001, around 8.00 a.m., as German intelligence sources report, in Exhibit 1D224, and in an OSCE report, Exhibit 1D12, Exhibit 1D23, 1D24, the so-called NLA launched a mortar attack on the Macedonian positions near the orthodox church in Ljuboten. The so-called NLA was the one that provoked the response and their goal was precisely this, to create an incident which the president wanted to avoid at all costs. After the three mortars exploded, the army responded with a barrage of mortar fire on identified targets in the village. Targets included sniper positions of the so-called NLA inside the village, machine-guns positions, and suspected mortar positions. This was confirmed by numerous Prosecution witnesses and documented evidence. The same will be confirmed by two credible Defence witnesses, one of them a professional army officer, who were based just above the village of Ljuboten and had an overall view of the events that followed. The Prosecution attempted to present evidence that in the early morning hours on Sunday, 12th August 2001, the village of Ljuboten and its residents were subject to an intense brutal and unlawful attack for which the accused are criminally responsible. The evidence has shown that the attack of the army and the police forces was proportionate, aimed only at the terrorists at the locations from where they were shooting at Macedonian positions, encouraged by the recent death of the Macedonian soldiers and the fact that NLA reinforcement was on the way to the village, only 500 metres from the south-eastern part. The evidence showed, and the Prosecution acknowledged in the indictment, that this NLA reinforcements consisted of two groups of NLA fighters, the so-called Arusha group and Teli group led by the notorious commander Xhezair Shaqiri Hoxha who tried to enter the village of Ljuboten but were stopped by the Macedonian army who spotted them and opened machine-gun and mortar fire resulting in the death of several members of the NLA. Unlike other places where the NLA was present - not all - no trenches were dug in Ljuboten for the simple reason that the security forces were present in the hills above Ljuboten and would have noticed it and also because of the location of Ljuboten. The village borders with villages that are populated by majority non-ethnic Albanians while the majority ethnic Albanian villages lie a further distance away to the north and the north-east. Non-ethnic Albanian population also lives in Ljuboten although their number is very small. Nonetheless, the extremists did not leave anything to chance and several days prior to the incident with the mine on 10th August, 2001, numerous trips were made by tractor to get sand from the Banjani mine, used to fill sandbags for fortifications; Exhibit 1D166. Also to emphasise the testimony of one of the Prosecution witnesses, M-051, who stated that there was at least one defensive position inside the village at that time. Your Honours, I would like now in brief to describe the NLA tactics when losing battles. In order to attract international attention and to boost the morale of its soldiers when all battles were lost the NLA described this either as a tactical withdrawal or that the deceased were not NLA members but innocent civilians. This was proved in the testimony of the Prosecution witness Mr. Nazim Bushi, who testified that NLA members who attacked the Macedonian positions near the stadium in Tetovo in March 2001 were civilians, although it was proven that they were in fact NLA members trying to throw a hand-grenade on a Macedonian check-point; Exhibit 2D49 and 2D51. This is relevant, Your Honours, because you will have to decide under what circumstances certain persons might have died or were injured. Also let us be reminded that up until the testimony of the present parents of Rami Jusufi the overall international public was informed that he was sleeping and that it was the blood thirsty Macedonians that killed him while he was in pyjamas. Confronted with material evidence, the parents several days before their testimony changed his statements and testified that he was not in pyjamas but that he had changed in jeans. Regarding the death of Rami Jusufi it must be emphasised that according to the post-mortem report and the expertise it would have been impossible for him to die in the manner described by his parents but that rather, he had to have been in a more elevated position; Exhibit 1D78. While the autopsy was performed, there were no signs of blood on the body; Exhibit 1D208. Your Honours, the Macedonian forces were fighting with a ghost armed group. One moment they were NLA fighters and were taking photographs like movie stars while at other moments they were innocent civilians whose rights were abused by the police. After the capture of Vaksince in May 2001, 200 strong men that fought in the village suddenly vanished after it was captured and only 150 civilians remained -- 1500 civilians remained. It was the NLA tactics to use civilians as human shields and to hide behind women and children when losing. This was reported and shown in several OSCE reports that had the most credible and independent information from the field; Exhibit 1D16. The same happened in Ljuboten. The terrorists who were shooting at the army and the police, once they felt they were losing the battle, became all of a sudden innocent civilians who hid in their basements with women and children. Some of them like Bajram Jashari, Kadri Bajrami and Xhelal Bajrami with their comrades from the Zendeli family tried to escape in the direction where the NLA reinforcement was but they were spotted and neutralised by the army. The other two managed to escape and join their comrades of the NLA and proudly took pictures as NLA members; Exhibit 2D21. Your Honours, the operation of the army and the police to dislodge the positions of the NLA was neither brutal nor intensive. It was proportional enough to crush the presence of the NLA in the village. It was not envisaged to abuse or harm civilians. Only selected houses in limited neighbourhoods were carefully targeted. These selected target houses were established as NLA positions. At the time of the attack, the village was full with villagers and civilians. The NLA was a threat to local villagers but also to everyone else around the village. The real culprits for what happened in the village are those members of the NLA who felt that it was acceptable to murder members of the army and then go and hide against civilians. The security forces entered only one house. The house that they entered, the Ametovski house, was the place where the Bajrami family was hiding. This family was a famous NLA family from where Shefajet Bajrami comes from; this is the person who planted the mine that killed eight Macedonian soldiers, as well as Rafet Bajrami comes from there. It was not by chance that they were found in this house. The security forces had credible information where they were hiding from Albanian sources in the village. This was the only house that was entered into. If the goal of the security forces had been to kill civilians, they would have entered all houses and would have killed anyone they might have found. Your Honour, the security forces, from 8.00 in the morning till 11.00, were unable to break the resistance that they faced at the entrance of Ljuboten from the western side, near the orthodox church. If there had been no NLA presence in the village, as the Prosecution claims, what were these forces doing in these locations for several hours? After the resistance was broken, the security forces proceeded in the direction of previously identified targets that were in the Ametovski house and then Jashari house, which were identified by Prosecution witnesses as houses where sniper and machine-gun fire came from. This will also be confirmed by Defence witnesses from the army. The two Defence witnesses will corroborate the Prosecution witnesses (redacted) and M-092; Exhibit P206 and P215, that after they escaped from the Jashari house, they were not spotted by the police forces on the ground but were spotted by the army positioned on Malistena or Smok, who opened fire on them and probably killed them. The Defence witnesses will testify that it was a legitimate military target because the Jashari house was a house identified by the army as a sniper and machine-gun position. Surely once the resistance of the NLA was being broken down, the NLA terrorists stationed in the Jashari house decided to flee towards the NLA positions above Ljuboten and became legitimate targets. From the same place, three pieces of weaponry were found and are now in the evidence of the Court. Your Honours, the theory of the Prosecution that those who entered the village intended to murder people presumes -- a presumption to that end cannot be drawn. Furthermore, the limited number of death casualties considering the intensity of the military exchange and of the terrorists in the village and of the security forces and the danger of this kind of urban fighting positively demonstrates that the death of these persons was related to combat activities and that they themselves took part in such activities. The other 2.000 Ljuboten villagers were left intact. If the intent of the group was to kill civilians, they would have gone house by house and killed everyone they would find in their way. No woman, no child or elderly person was touched or hurt or searched. As a fact, a battalion of posebna was sent to save from the local villagers and efforts were made for them to be taken to safety. The whole operation ended around noon. The forces that entered the village after less than an hour withdrew, once they neutralized the NLA positions located at and near the Jashari house. The civilians that were held hostage by the terrorists left in the direction of Skopje. As I explained previously, the tactics of the NLA was to dress themselves in civilian clothing after they were defeated. This is why the police detained Ljuboten villagers and only those with a positive paraffin glove test were brought before an investigating judge and before justice, while those with a negative paraffin glove test were released. Mr. Tarculovski did not have any information about the development of this operation and did not have any authority to communicate or to control the involved parties. Your Honours, now I would like to speak about the alleged criminal liability of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. It is the duty of the Prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused Tarculovski is responsible pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute for the crimes described in the Second Amended Indictment. The Prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Johan is guilty for the charges. The Defence acknowledges that Mr. Tarculovski was present in Ljubanci during the events, and he does not deny this. He was there upon a very clear order of the president to monitor the situation and to inform him. Furthermore, he was there to convey messages to the members of the army and the police that were on the field and this was a practice which was very frequently used by the president and this was confirmed by the witness Keskovski. He was also sent by the president to other locations. His presence was legal, because it stemmed out of a direct order of the president. The Prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt and the Defence will not give evidence about the participation of the accused Tarculovski in the joint criminal enterprise together with several other individuals. The Prosecution did not prove that anyone had agreed to commit crimes, let alone to commit crimes that are charged. The Prosecutor failed to prove that anybody participated in such an operation. It is a fact and is contrary to the allegations that those that were involved had the same legitimate intention in mind, to conduct anti-terrorist operation with an aim to avoid further attacks from the NLA as such. This deed, as it is defined in the Second Amended Indictment does not exist. The Prosecution claims without evidence that the object of this enterprise was a direct and unlawful attack on civilians and civilian objects in the village of Ljuboten, which could not be justified with military necessity. The action of the Macedonian police and the army was legal and legitimate. It was ordered by the late President Trajkovski to defend the Macedonian villages near Ljuboten and to destroy the NLA positions in and around Ljuboten. The army and the police had reliable information that the village of Ljuboten was under the NLA control and all the activities were directed towards destroying the NLA in the village. As stated before, only carefully selected NLA positions were targeted and civilian population of about 2.000 civilians left unharmed. The Prosecution failed to prove that there existed a common plan, a design and a purpose, as element of the JCE. The alleged existence of the joint criminal enterprise is a legal construction without solid grounds in the evidence. The Prosecution did not lead evidence about the alleged participation of Johan in such a plan. The Prosecution failed to establish that Johan knew of such an enterprise, and the evidence do not leave any doubts that the operation was legitimate and that all involved parties knew and were convinced that there was presence of NLA in the village which was a danger that needed to be eliminated. The village and the villagers were never a target. The Prosecution failed to present evidence who were the other members of the joint criminal enterprise and who their role was. The reason for this is very simple: There was no joint criminal enterprise, and there were no members of the joint criminal enterprise. There is no evidence that the individuals alleged to have been members of that joint criminal enterprise, as identified in the Prosecution pre-trial brief had any part in crime, let alone the crimes they are charged with. Even more, the Prosecution failed to lead evidence to prove beyond reasonable doubt the alleged mens rea of the accused. With the regard of the first type of the joint criminal enterprise, the Prosecution failed to lead evidence whether Johan shared intent with others to murder and to treat civilians in a cruel manner, nor to wantonly destroy villages or cities. In regards with the third type of the joint criminal enterprise, the Prosecution failed to lead evidence and failed to prove that the accused had sufficient knowledge that the alleged additional crimes were a natural and foreseeable consequence of the primary plan, which, according to the indictment, was to conduct unlawful attack on civilians and civilian objects in the village of Ljuboten. Surely the accused Tarculovski was there upon the request of the president to monitor, to inform him, and to send messages to the army and police chiefs. That was an order that he could not refuse coming from the supreme commander of the armed forces. Unfortunately, President Trajkovski passed away and cannot help this Chamber in confirming the truth. However, one Prosecution witness, Mr. Despodov, and one witness of Boskoski, Mr. Keskovski, testified that Johan was the messenger between the army and the president. There was no order or agreement to commit any crime but there was an intent to avoid any further crimes that the so-called NLA may commit. The authorities, especially the president, were convinced that NLA members were in the village and that was the reason why the president ordered the operation so as to avoid that NLA could organise any further operations that would impede the signing of the Ohrid Agreement on the 13th of August, 2001. Regarding his alleged criminal liability through planning, the Prosecution did not lead any evidence in that point, and they failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Mr. Tarculovski planned or designed preparatory and executive phases of the criminal conduct, constituting some of the crimes he is charged with in the Second Amended Indictment. In fact the Prosecutor failed to demonstrate that Mr. Tarculovski played any part in committing of any of the crimes that he is charged with, and therefore, the Prosecutor failed to prove that Mr. Tarculovski acted with an intent what crime should be committed or with awareness of the substantial likelihood the crime will be committed in the execution of that plan. Indeed this was legal joint operation by the Macedonian army and the police to destroy terrorists that were based in the village of Ljuboten. Neither did Johan control nor command anyone in Ljuboten. Not one single alleged perpetrator has been identified. Johan never associated himself with any of the alleged perpetrators which the Prosecutor failed to identify and failed to prove to be criminals. I'm not going to speak about the charges in the second amended indictment regarding the alleged criminal liability of the accused Tarculovski in instigating, ordering, aiding and abetting as charged in the second amended indictment, due to the fact that the Prosecution made no effort to prove any of the above-mentioned forms of perpetration. If the Prosecution tried to establish this, then the Prosecution completely failed. Your Honours, this is a very strange case and indictment. We are not going to try to evaluate the political reasons why the Prosecution decided to prosecute only the Ljuboten case and decided not to prosecute clear cases of ethnic cleansing, rape, murder and torture perpetrated by the NLA members; yet the Prosecution decided to indict those who tried and succeeded in defending Macedonia, those that had the courage to stand up and confront the terrorist threat that threatened to destroy democratic Macedonia. We should mention here the one-sided partial and non-professional report of Mr. Bouckaert which was sent to international organisations and the media. His intentions maybe were not dishonest, but his approach was. His conclusions are wrong. His methodology was wrong. His unpreparedness to hear the side of the Macedonian authors was wrong. He was one-sided and his attempt to give Mr. Boskoski the only responsibility was wrong. His idea to be an investigator, a judge and to decide the trial in just one week by deciding that the Macedonian security forces are guilty and then by sending the sensational news to all international media was completely wrong. This report totally disregards the findings of the OSCE, the International Crisis Group, the EU Monitoring Mission, the International Committee of Red Cross and other relevant international organisations. In this modern world of communication all news broadcast via the media are accepted and the media have become the ultimate judge. Fortunately, the international justice is still in the hands of experienced lawyers who are trained and able to impartially assess the evidence and witnesses in reaching just verdict. Your Honours, this is a historical case for Macedonia. This case will either give legitimacy to the security forces of Macedonia in defending the sovereignty of Macedonia or will award the terrorists who tried to destroy the constitutional order of the Republic of Macedonia, member of the United Nations. We have full faith that this Trial Chamber will reach a just verdict and that being to acquit the accused Tarculovski. The acquittal will not only be fair but the only fair thing to do. Thank you, Your Honours, for listening to my opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed, Mr. Apostolski, for the comprehensive approach you have taken to the issues. That concludes what is planned to be dealt with today. We, therefore, adjourn now, with a view to the evidence that you will be leading, commencing tomorrow, and we are sitting tomorrow in the morning, I hope has been noticed, and in another courtroom. So that we adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow.
